source_text: Τὸ μὲν οὖν ἄθεοι μὴ εἶναι, ἕνα τὸν ἀγένητον καὶ ἀΐδιον καὶ ἀόρατον καὶ ἀπαθῆ καὶ ἀκατάληπτον καὶ ἀχώρητον, νῷ μόνῳ καὶ λόγῳ καταλαμβανόμενον, φωτὶ καὶ κάλλει καὶ πνεύματι καὶ δυνάμει ἀνεκδιηγήτῳ περιεχόμενον, ὑφ᾿ οὗ γεγένηται τὸ πᾶν διὰ τοῦ αὐτοῦ λόγου καὶ διακεκόσμηται καὶ συγκρατεῖται, θεὸν ἄγοντες, ἱκανῶς μοι δέδεικται. Νοοῦμεν γὰρ καὶ υἱὸν τοῦ θεοῦ. Καὶ μή μοι γελοῖόν τις νομίσῃ τὸ υἱὸν εἶναι τῷ θεῷ. Οὐ γὰρ ὡς ποιηταὶ μυθοποιοῦσιν, οὐδὲν βελτίους τῶν ἀνθρώπων δεικνῦντες τοὺς θεούς, ἢ περὶ τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ πατρὸς ἢ περὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ πεφρονήκαμεν. Ἀλλ᾿ ἔστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ λόγος τοῦ πατρὸς ἐν ἰδέᾳ καὶ ἐνεργείᾳ· πρὸς αὐτοῦ γὰρ καὶ δι᾿ αὐτοῦ πάντα ἐγένετο, ἑνὸς ὄντος τοῦ πατρὸς καὶ τοῦ υἱοῦ. Ὄντος δὲ τοῦ υἱοῦ ἐν πατρὶ καὶ πατρὸς ἐν υἱῷ, ἑνότητι καὶ δυνάμει πνεύματος, νοῦς καὶ λόγος τοῦ πατρὸς ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ. Εἰ δὲ δι᾿ ὑπερβολὴν συνέσεως σκοπεῖν ὑμῖν ἔπεισιν, ὁ παῖς τί βούλεται, ἐρῶ διὰ βραχέων πρῶτον γέννημα εἶναι τῷ πατρί, οὐχ ὡς γενόμενον (ἐξ ἀρχῆς γὰρ ὁ θεός, νοῦς ἀΐδιος ὤν, εἶχεν αὐτὸς ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὸν λόγον, ἀϊδίως λογικὸς ὤν), ἀλλ᾿ ὡς τῶν ὑλικῶν ξυμπάντων, ἀποίου φύσεως καὶ γῆς ἀχρείας ὑποκειμένων δίκην, μεμιγμένων τῶν παχυμερεστέρων πρὸς τὰ κουφότερα ἐπ᾿ αὐτοῖς, ἰδέα καὶ ἐνέργεια εἶναι προελθών. Συνᾴδει δὲ τῷ λόγῳ καὶ τὸ προφητικὸν πνεῦμα· Κύριος γάρ, φησίν, ἔκτισέ με ἀρχὴν ὁδῶν αὐτοῦ εἰς ἔργα αὐτοῦ. Καίτοι καὶ αὐτὸ τὸ ἐνεργοῦν τοῖς ἐκφωνοῦσι προφητικῶς ἅγιον πνεῦμα ἀπόῤῥοιαν εἶναί φαμεν τοῦ θεοῦ, ἀποῤῥέον καὶ ἐπαναφερόμενον ὡς ἀκτῖνα ἡλίου.Τίς οὖν οὐκ ἂν ἀπορήσαι, λέγοντας θεὸν πατέρα καὶ υἱὸν θεὸν καὶ πνεῦμα ἅγιον, δεικνύντας αὐτῶν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ ἑνώσει δύναμιν καὶ τὴν ἐν τῇ τάξει διαίρεσιν, ἀκούσας ἀθέους καλουμένους; Καὶ οὐκ ἐπὶ τούτοις τὸ θεολογικὸν ἡμῶν ἵσταται μέρος· ἀλλὰ καὶ πλῆθος ἀγγέλων καὶ λειτουργῶν φαμεν, οὓς ὁ ποιητὴς καὶ δημιουργὸς κόσμου θεὸς διὰ τοῦ παρ᾿ αὐτοῦ λόγου διένειμε καὶ διέταξε περί τε τὰ στοιχεῖα εἶναι καὶ τοὺς οὐρανοὺς καὶ τὸν κόσμον καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτῷ καὶ τὴν τούτων εὐταξίαν.
pass_a_gloss: That therefore we are not atheists, one unborn and eternal and invisible and impassive and incomprehensible and uncircumscribed, being apprehended by mind alone and reason, being encompassed by light and beauty and spirit and indescribable power, by whom all things have been made through his own word and have been adorned and are held together, having been shown to me sufficiently. For we think also of the Son of God. And let no one think it laughable that the Son is to God. For not as poets mythologize, showing the gods to be no better than men, nor have we thought about God and Father or about the Son. But the Son of God is the reason of the Father in idea and in energy; for through him and on account of him all things have been made, the Father and the Son being one. And the Son being in the Father and the Father in the Son, by unity and power of spirit, the Son of God is the mind and reason of the Father. And if because of excess of intelligence it seems to you to be examining, what the child wants, I will say briefly that he is the firstborn to the Father, not as having been made (for God was from the beginning, being an eternal mind, having the reason in himself eternally, being eternally rational), but as the idea and energy have proceeded before the material substances, of a divine nature and useless earth lying beneath, the thicker mixed with the thinner upon them. And the prophetic spirit agrees with the reason; for the Lord, it says, created me the beginning of his ways for his works. And also the holy spirit that energizes those who speak prophetically, we say is an effluence of God, flowing out and being referred back like a ray of the sun. Who then would not be at a loss, speaking of God the Father and Son of God and Holy Spirit, showing both their power in unity and their distinction in order, having been called atheists? And our theological part is not established on these things; but we also say a multitude of angels and ministers, whom the creator and maker of the world God distributed and ordered through his own word, concerning both the elements and the heavens and the world and the things in it and their good order.

choices.why: referring to those who do not believe in God
referring to the third person of the Trinity

bible_refs.note: Lord created me the beginning of his ways

pass_b_english: I have sufficiently demonstrated that we are not atheists, for we worship one God who is unbegotten, eternal, invisible, impassible, incomprehensible, and uncircumscribed. He is apprehended only by mind and reason, and encompassed by light, beauty, spirit, and indescribable power. Through his own Word, he has made, adorned, and holds together all things. We also acknowledge the Son of God; let no one consider it laughable that God has a Son. We do not think as the poets who mythologize, portraying gods no better than men; our conception of God the Father and the Son is altogether different. The Son of God is the Father's Reason (Logos) in idea and actuality. Through him and because of him all things came to be, for the Father and the Son are one. Since the Son is in the Father and the Father in the Son, united by the unity and power of the Spirit, the Son of God is the Mind and Reason of the Father. If, in excess of cleverness, you demand to know what the 'Child' desires, I will answer briefly: he is the Father's firstborn, not as one who came into existence. From the beginning God, being an eternal Mind, possessed his own Reason within himself, being eternally rational. Rather, the Son proceeded as Idea and Energy before material substances existed, when divine nature and useless earth lay beneath, the heavier elements mixed with the lighter upon them. The prophetic Spirit agrees with this Reason, saying, "The Lord created me the beginning of his ways for his works" (Proverbs 8:22). We also declare that the Holy Spirit who energizes those who speak prophetically is an effluence of God, flowing out and returning like a ray of the sun. Who would not be perplexed to hear us called atheists when we proclaim God the Father, God the Son, and the Holy Spirit, demonstrating both their power in unity and their distinction in order? Our theology does not rest on these truths alone; we also affirm a multitude of angels and ministers. The Creator and Maker of the world, God, distributed and ordered them through his own Word to govern the elements, the heavens, the world, all things in it, and their harmonious arrangement.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the complex theological distinctions of the Greek text, including the distinction between the eternal nature of the Logos and its relation to material substances. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek. The scripture citation (Proverbs 8:22) is correctly identified in Pass B and matches the Greek allusion.
